budget: Enforce ledger transition-completeness at append time so an append-side tail-strip cannot be silently re-anchored, closing the codex P2 deferred from the TASK-20260724-019 panel (.review-store/t019-codex-review-b141afd.txt:31; Linear META-31). Threat boundary: hash-chaining proves the INTEGRITY of records that are present; it cannot prove COMPLETENESS. Stripping a ledger tail leaves a structurally valid, shorter chain, and the next legitimate append re-anchors prevEntryHash across the gap so every later validation passes. This card makes that gap detectable at the moment of the next append. Exactly one behavioral change plus its tests, both inside the two reserved paths. (1) In appendReceipt (scripts/workplan.mjs:1304-1331), before the new record is built, enforce the invariant tail.to === from, where tail is the last element of card.receipts and from is the argument ALREADY PASSED to appendReceipt. The comparison MUST use the from argument and MUST NOT read card.status: card.status is mutated BEFORE appendReceipt at 5 of the 9 call sites (claim 1456 before 1459, claim-next 1553 before 1556, accept 2445 before 2463, block 2649 before 2651, ready 2875 before 2881) and AFTER it at the other 4 (start 1888 before 1896, submit 1975 before 1984, integrate 2092 before 2106, resume 2761 before 2771), so any implementation reading card.status is wrong at half the sites. The from argument is the true pre-transition status at all 9 sites, including block, where from = card.blockedFrom is captured at 2646 before card.status is overwritten at 2649. (2) Legacy tolerance, stated exactly: tolerate ABSENCE, never MISMATCH. A card whose receipts array is absent or empty passes (genesis; also the seeded bootstrap card TASK-20260714-001, which is done with no receipts key on the live board). When a tail EXISTS the invariant is enforced regardless of whether that tail carries entryHash - legacy un-chained records are still records, and a fully legacy ledger is exactly where this attack is cheapest. The rejected weaker alternative, enforcing only when the tail is chained, would leave the entire live board (zero chained records today) undefended. (3) Placement inside appendReceipt is load-bearing, not cosmetic: it is the single choke point through which all 9 append sites funnel, card.receipts is already resident so no new I/O is needed, and because the three commands that already carry receipts-relevant checks run them first (accept validateIntegrationReceipt 2416 and validateReceiptChain 2417 before 2463; block validateReceiptChain 2635 before 2651; resume the latestReceipt.to !== blocked guard 2738, validateBlockedReceipt 2740 and validateReceiptChain 2748 before 2761) the new check can never displace an existing error message. The other 6 commands carry no pre-existing receipts checks, so the new check is simply the first such check there. Hoisting this as a blanket pre-check at command entry is FORBIDDEN: it would break the assertions at scripts/workplan.test.mjs:8001, :8789 and :6786, each of which deliberately constructs a tail/status mismatch and asserts on the existing narrower message. (4) On violation, fail() with a distinct greppable message; the frozen wording is: ledger tail <tail.to> does not match transition from <from>. Regression tests in scripts/workplan.test.mjs following existing conventions (repository/state/card builders :33-81, reachVerifying :349-381, blockCard :383-411, resumeCard :413-430): (a) THE CODEX REPRO EXACTLY - legitimately reach claimed, strip the ready-to-claimed record, run start, and assert it fails with the new message; this is the card reason to exist; (b) the same strip shape on a fully legacy un-chained ledger also fails; (c) genesis regression - a card with no receipts key still goes ready cleanly (guarding :8195); (d) an empty receipts array on a non-backlog card is allowed, pinned explicitly because no existing test covers that shape; (e) happy-path per transition - ready, claim, start, submit, integrate, block, resume all still append normally with a consistent tail; (f) block from review passes the check via blockedFrom; (g) resume from blocked passes with tail.to === blocked; (h) byte-preservation - state.json is unchanged after a rejected transition, mirroring the existing preserves-bytes pattern.
stopCondition: Stop and fail closed on: any edit outside the two reserved paths (scripts/workplan.mjs, scripts/workplan.test.mjs); any implementation that reads card.status instead of the from argument inside appendReceipt; any hoisting of the new check to command entry or to validateState; any rewrite, re-hash, deletion or reordering of ledger records already present in a state file - append-only is inviolable; any check that rejects a card with an absent or empty receipts array; any weakening, rewording or deletion of an existing assertion in scripts/workplan.test.mjs to make the new check fit - if an existing test genuinely conflicts, STOP and report rather than edit it; any change to the declared residual pinned at scripts/workplan.test.mjs:8877, which strips chain FIELDS but no RECORD and must keep passing untouched; any edit to development/remote_workplan/gateway.py or any other file the trace mentions but the paths do not reserve; any new CLI flag, subcommand or dependency; validation ordered after mutation; a failing acceptance command; or an unresolved P0/P1 review finding.
